claim:model-connectivity.proposition: Model Connectivity Network — How the Curated Models Couple

narrative.question:
Having trusted the models (Act 1), given them an anatomical address (Act 2),
and measured their 3D coverage (Act 3): do the curated models actually form a
connected network through shared biological content — which variables do they
share, how densely do they couple, and is there a mechanistic backbone, or
just isolated islands?

units.proposition: Model Connectivity Network — How the Curated Models Couple

decisions.title: Shared-identifier edges mark candidate couplings; which of the densest edges are actually mechanistically composable (compatible units/rate laws)?
decisions.detail: The network finds where models share species, not whether they can be wired together — the natural next step is to validate the strongest edges as real process-bigraph compositions.

decisions.title: Should the connectivity backbone drive a prioritized model-composition roadmap (which hub models to compose first)?
decisions.detail: The dominant 634-model component around ATP/translation suggests energy-metabolism hubs as composition seeds; this is a strategy decision for the multi-model program.
